subject: Endpoint economics: per-endpoint cost & latency snapshot request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Endpoint economics: per-endpoint cost & latency snapshot request

Team —

For next week's product review & an ask from Sales, I need an ad-hoc breakdown that shows cost and latency by endpoint (per-route/per-API-path) for the hosted Console traffic over the last 30 days. High level asks: 

- Per-endpoint tokens and compute cost (approximate $) for the last 30 days
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and median payload sizes by endpoint
- Identify the top 10 endpoints by cost and the top 10 by tail latency (can overlap)
- Mark any endpoints where caching/batching would have >20% potential cost savings (rough estimate)

I've attached a tiny sample of queries and the mockup I sketched (current-query-sample.csv, endpoint-mockup.png). This is primarily for the exec review on Sep 10 — can we get an initial table + 3-slide summary by end of day Monday (Sep 7)?

If there are constraints (data availability, sampling needed, permissions) call them out and propose a minimal deliverable. If we can do a quick canary for ACME (ops@acme-data.com) that would be great — they're curious about how their routes compare.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Endpoint economics: per-endpoint cost & latency snapshot request

Ack — thanks for the brief. A few quick Qs so we scope correctly: 

1) Cost model: do you want proxied token-cost only (hosted metering) or token + infra (GPU hours amortized)? The latter needs infra cost mapping that is slightly delayed in our billing pipeline.
2) Time window: 30 days rolling ending today? or Sep 1–30 (calendar month)?
3) Level: path-level (e.g., /v1/generate) vs route-level including route metadata (customer_id, plan)?

My suggestion for Monday: we can deliver a route-level CSV with estimated per-route token cost (using hosted token rates) + p50/p95/p99 latency. If you want infra amortization, we can add that as a follow-up (should be ready by Sep 13).

I'll take the lead on pulling the metrics, but I'll need Neha to extract endpoint identifiers and Grace for product approval on sharing any customer-labeled routes externally.

—Logan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Endpoint economics: per-endpoint cost & latency snapshot request

Vanessa / Logan —

We can generate this. A few technical notes / constraints to set expectations: 

- The current telemetry schema has route_id, model_variant, and token_count at the request level. We don't consistently persist per-token compute-time per request; we estimate compute cost by mapping token_count x model profile (avg ms/token). That works for hosted API routes.
- Sampling: we can sample 10% of requests for full latency percentiles to speed extraction; full-window p99 at 0.1% tail needs more runtime to compute but doable if we raise the job priority.
- Customer-labeled routes: we need product sign-off to include customer IDs in slides. Otherwise we can anonymize as "cust-1, cust-2" and highlight examples.

I'll prepare a CSV that includes: route_id, anon_customer, token_count_sum, est_cost_usd, p50, p95, p99, median_payload_bytes, model_variant. Attaching a quick query sample (current-query-sample.csv) — same file you attached but augmented with route IDs for example.

If we want caching/batching savings estimates, I'll run a heuristic that looks at repeated prefixes and KV-cache hits across requests; that will add ~48 hours if we want to be thorough.

-Neha

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 06 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Endpoint economics: per-endpoint cost & latency snapshot request

Vanessa —

Product prioritization note: the Console team can't commit to a new dashboard UI by next week, but we can do an internal ad-hoc report + a lightweight visual (1 slide) that summarizes top endpoints by cost and tail latency. We'll need to confirm that we can share anonymized customer IDs externally; Legal asked to avoid customer-identifiable data without consent. If ACME wants a canary, we should spin an anonymized snapshot first and then loop them in for a meeting.

Deliverables we'll commit to for Monday EOD (Sep 7):
- CSV with per-route estimates (see Neha's column list)
- 1-slide visual for execs (top 10 cost, top 10 tail latency)
- Short note on assumptions and limitations (sampling rate, cost model)

If Vanessa / Sales want more (infra amortization, caching analysis), we'll schedule a follow-up with an ETA (by Sep 13).

Grace

Subject: Re: Endpoint economics: per-endpoint cost & latency snapshot request

Thanks all — that plan works. Two small asks before you run the job: 

1) Please anonymize customer IDs in the public slides; include a separate CSV column with a reversible hash we can share with Sales for mapping (so Legal is OK).
2) For the p99 numbers, please flag any endpoint where p99 exceeds 1.5x the p95 — we want to call out high-tail instability.

Logan / Neha: include a short README in the Drive folder describing sampling and cost assumptions. Once you have the anonymized snapshot, ACME (copied) can look and we can set a 30-min sync on Tue Sep 8 if they want to review.

Appreciate the quick turn — I'll prep the slide deck.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
